title: Police planted knife; ID of cop who shot husband disputed
article: An Amherstburg police officer planted a knife as evidence shortly after Robert Scott Carpenter was shot by an off-duty police officer, Carpenter's widow alleged at a coroner's inquest Wednesday.

The allegations made by Lisa Stewart are at odds with the sequence of events outlined for the jury by coroner's counsel Robert Ash. They also appear to contradict statements Stewart allegedly made to investigators following the Oct. 30 shooting.
Stewart told the three-man and two-women jury that an unidentified police officer planted the knife after an unarmed Carpenter was shot by Sgt. Bart DiPasquale.

After describing what the officer looked like, Stewart announced he was at the inquest. She left the witness box at Ash's request and tapped the officer on the shoulder. He stood and identified himself as Const. Viktor Burany.
The jury was told by Ash on Tuesday that Carpenter set upon DiPasquale with a knife in the front foyer of his 258 McCurdy Dr. home and was shot by Const. Shawn McCurdy.
McCurdy was in uniform but DiPasquale was not.
Stewart testified DiPasquale fired the fatal bullet from a gold- or brass- coloured weapon pulled from the area around his left thigh.
The evidence is consistent with transcripts of an interview given by Stewart last Nov. 14 to a student working for Windsor lawyer Patrick Ducharme.

Finn Nielsen, a firearms and toolmarkings expert with the Centre of Forensic Sciences in Toronto, testified the bullet removed from the upper right leg of Carpenter matched test bullets fired from McCurdy's service pistol -- a .40 caliber Smith and Wesson, serial number VAU2246.
Asked if the fatal bullet could have been fired by a .38 calibre Smith and Wesson revolver registered to DiPasquale, Nielsen said, "It's impossible."

Stewart was adamant Wednesday Carpenter never attacked DiPasquale with a knife. She said he had been carrying the knife in the hours before the shooting but had placed it on the fridge before police arrived.

Stewart maintained that Burany took the knife from the fridge and placed it on the ground after the shooting. She said the hinged knife was only partially opened and was not marked with blood. Photographs investigators took of the scene show a knife with a fully-extended blade covered with what appears to be blood.

Forensics investigator David Klodt said the knife was bagged at the scene but never analysed for fingerprints. He added knife handles aren't the best surfaces for lifting fingerprints. The knife was only recently sent for analysis at Ash's request.

In an interview conducted by investigators the day of the shooting, according to portions of transcripts read aloud Wednesday, Stewart makes several references to Carpenter being armed with a knife. The transcripts also indicate Stewart told McCurdy Carpenter may have been armed with a knife.

Stewart denied making that comment to McCurdy and denied making many of the statements attributed to her by investigators in that initial interview. She never wavered in her conviction Carpenter wasn't armed with a knife and that he was shot by DiPasquale.
Ash was to resume questioning Stewart this morning.
